Credit Controller

The Role

Reporting to the Credit Manager, you will be responsible for managing outstanding debt, resolving payment issues and ensuring customer accounts are maintained accurately and in line with agreed payment terms.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing the end to end collection of outstanding debt across an allocated ledger, ensuring payments are received within agreed terms.
- Proactively monitoring aged debt, reducing overdue balances and escalating high risk accounts where appropriate.
- Building and maintaining strong relationships with clients and internal stakeholders to support timely payment and effective query resolution.
- Investigating and resolving invoice, purchase order and billing disputes to remove barriers to payment.
- Working with senior stakeholders to highlight collection issues, agree action plans and drive outstanding balances through to resolution.
- Providing regular updates on collection performance, aged debt and potential bad debt exposure.
- Supporting accurate account management, cash allocation, reporting and forecasting.
- Identifying opportunities to improve credit control processes and collection performance.

About You

You will have proven experience in credit control and debt collection, with a track record of managing outstanding debt and achieving cash collection targets.

You will also demonstrate:
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build productive relationships at all levels.
- Experience investigating and resolving invoice, PO and billing disputes.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy when reconciling accounts and maintaining customer records.
- Strong Excel skills, including VLOOKUP and PivotTables, to support debt analysis and reporting.
- A proactive and organised approach, with the confidence to manage competing priorities and take ownership of collection activity.

What's on Offer
- Salary of £30,000 to £36,000, depending on experience.
- Hybrid working, with 2 days in the office and 3 days working from home.
- The opportunity to join an established Finance team within a professional services environment.
- A varied role with ownership of a ledger and regular interaction with key stakeholders.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
- Payroll Administrator
- 6 Month FTC
- £27-33k, hybrid, immediate start

Payroll Administrator
This is a six month contract supporting a business through a big payroll change, as they move onto a brand new payroll system. You'll be part of the payroll team, brought in to test the new system before it goes live, so it's a great chance to see a full payroll transformation from the inside. It's full time at 37.5 hours, hybrid with just 1-2 days a week in the Birmingham city centre office, and pays £27,000 to £33,000 depending on experience.
You'll be an experienced Payroll Administrator who knows payroll well enough to spot straight away when something isn't right. You're methodical, you like checking things properly, and you're happy to raise a hand when a result doesn't add up. Just as importantly, you're available now or very soon, because they want someone in seat straight away.

What You Will Be Doing
- Joining the payroll team to support the move from an older payroll system onto a brand new one, as part of a fixed-term project.
- Supporting user acceptance testing, working through test scenarios to make sure the new system does what payroll actually needs it to do.
- Testing how data from other systems feeds into payroll, checking that hours and pay come through correctly.
- Checking test results against what you'd expect to see, using your payroll knowledge to spot anything that looks off.
- Logging issues clearly and following them up, so problems are fixed before go-live rather than after.
- Helping check that data moved across from the old system has landed correctly in the new one.
- Working closely with the Payroll Manager, who will be your go-to for direction.
- Using your Excel skills to compare, check and pull together data throughout testing.
- Making sure what you test lines up with HMRC rules and the way payroll needs to run day to day.
- Keeping testing moving to tight project deadlines, with a fixed go-live date that everyone is working towards.

What We Need From You
- Solid hands-on payroll experience, enough that you know exactly what a correct result should look like. CIPP membership would be a bonus, but it isn't a must.
- You don't need experience of the new system. If you've been through a payroll system change, data migration or testing before, that will help you hit the ground running.
- Someone methodical who takes real pride in accuracy. Anything missed in testing ends up in real people's pay, so your attention to detail genuinely matters here.
- Confident enough to question things. If a result doesn't look right, you'll say so rather than assume it's fine.
- Comfortable working in Excel at an intermediate level, confident checking and comparing data.
- Calm under pressure. Project deadlines don't move, and you keep a clear head when it gets busy.
- A clear, organised communicator who works well with payroll colleagues, HR and the wider project team.
- Immediately available or on a very short notice period, as they're looking for someone to start straight away.

What's in it for you
- A salary of £27,000 to £33,000 depending on experience.
- Hybrid working, with just 1-2 days a week in the office.
- A city centre base in Birmingham, easy to reach by public transport.
- An immediate start on a clearly defined six month contract.
- A full payroll system go-live on your CV, which is real, marketable project experience.
- Hands-on testing experience, a really useful skill as more businesses move onto new payroll systems.

If you know your payroll inside out and like the idea of helping a new system go live the right way, apply today and let's have a chat.

title: Credit Controller
description:
An exceptional opportunity has arisen for a highly experienced, autonomous Credit Controller to assume ownership of a high-profile ledger within a leading, multi-site food production and manufacturing organisation based in Solihull. This is a fast-paced, high-volume environment designed for a seasoned professional who thrives under pressure, enjoys managing sophisticated corporate accounts, and possesses a natural flair for advanced query resolution.

This dynamic role requires you to proactively chase outstanding balances via phone and email, accurately allocate complex, multi-currency incoming cash across the ledger, and perform detailed account reconciliations. You will frequently investigate and resolve intricate invoice and delivery disputes, partnering closely with internal commercial and distribution teams to dismantle payment barriers. Regularly analysing aged debt reports to flag financial risks and reporting key performance metrics to senior management will also form a critical part of your daily routine.

- Advanced query resolution skills with the ability to navigate complex distribution and invoicing discrepancies.
- Exceptional negotiation and communication capabilities to manage high-value stakeholder relationships.
- Advanced technical literacy including strong Excel skills and proficiency in major ERP software.

What You Will Receive

- Premium exposure to massive, high-profile corporate financial ledgers that will significantly elevate your interim career profile.
- Highly collaborative team environment with a welcoming office culture and a comprehensive, fast-tracked on boarding process.
- Clear temp-to-perm progression pathway offering the opportunity to transition into a secure, long-term permanent position for the right candidate.

If you are a driven, career-minded Credit Controller looking for a high-impact, fast-moving role where your expertise will be recognised and rewarded from day one, we would love to hear from you, apply today and take the next step in your financial career.

title: Finance Assistant - Maternity Cover
description:
Job Title: Finance Assistant

Location: Mason Court, Hillborough Road, Olton, Solihull

Salary: £25,000 per annum

Job Type: Full Time, 12 months fixed term contract to cover maternity.

About Mason Yardley Trust:

As a charity, MY Trust is dedicated to making a positive impact on the lives of individuals and families. With roots dating back nearly 700 years, as Sir Josiah Mason Trust and Yardley Great Trust, our legacy is one of compassion, inclusivity, trust and excellence.

Our vision is a future where all people have a great place to call home, are part of a thriving community and have opportunities to achieve their potential. Our family of charities strive to improve lives and create opportunities by providing quality homes, care, support, and education.

We value our hardworking, loyal staff and believe that our people make us who we are. We provide rewarding training opportunities for all of our staff and encourage them to reach their potential and make the best use of their skills and abilities.

About the role:

As a Finance Assistant your role purpose will be to support the Director of Finance & IT in maintaining the financial ledgers of the Trust. Within your role, you will be required to facilitate the smooth operation of systems and procedures.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

Financial Accounting:
- To maintain the SJMT Purchase Ledgers on a daily basis by:-
- Matching orders and delivery notes to invoices
- Liaising with budget holders to ensure all necessary documentation is authorised
- Coding and posting invoices
- Pay suppliers by BACS in accordance with their terms of payment
- Reconciling purchase ledger accounts
- To maintain the SJMT Sales Ledgers on a daily basis by:-
- Raising monthly sales invoices
- Receive and bank cash and cheque contributions, fees and sundry income from residents, keeping accurate records of such receipts
- Reconciling sales ledger control accounts
- To maintain the SJMT Rent Ledger on a daily basis by posting receipts on a daily basis.
- To reconcile the SJMT bank accounts on a monthly basis.
- To check, balance and re-imburse petty cash floats as appropriate.
- To administer the credit card process
- To provide support for inter charity reconciliations
- To process the works orders on the Omni systems for YGT and TYC charities and close down once invoices are received.

Other Duties:
- To liaise with staff and residents as necessary to carry out duties and responsibilities.
- To comply with financial standing orders and procedures.
- To assist in maintaining financial and administration systems.
- To undertake any other duties reasonably requested by the Director of Finance and IT or Management Accountant.

About you:

Experience:
- Knowledge of double entry book keeping, control account reconciliation, and bank account reconciliation.
- At least 1 year experience using computerised accounting systems
- SAGE 50 Accounts experience (Desirable)

Skills & abilities:
- Methodic.
- Accurate.
- Ability to work to targets.
- Likes working in a team.
- Problem solver.
- Curious.
- Willing to use own initiative.

Education/ qualifications:
- Part 1 AAT or first level other accountancy qualification or qualified by experience
- Looking to complete AAT or other qualification (Desirable)

Other:
- Ability to communicate with people at all levels including residents, relatives, managers, staff, suppliers.
- Awareness of diversity issues and works in a positive non-discriminatory way.
- Enhanced DBS check will be taken up

Benefits:
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Blue Light Card

Please click the APPLY button to send a CV for this role.

Candidates with previous experience and job titles of; Accounts Assistant, Accounts Assistant, Finance Clerk, Accounts Clerk, Finance Officer Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable Assistant, Billing Assistant, Payroll Assistant, Finance Support Officer, may also be considered for this role.
